request.question: Explain what a Python dictionary is, with one short example.

feedback.samjho: A Python dictionary is a collection of key-value pairs. Each key is unique and used to access its associated value. For example, {'name': 'Sam', 'city': 'Delhi'} stores name and city. You can retrieve a value using the key, like dict['name'].
feedback.answer_likho:
A Python dictionary is a data structure that stores key-value pairs. Each key is unique and maps to a value. It is useful for organizing data where you need to look up values by a specific identifier.

Example: {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 25} — here, 'name' maps to 'Alice' and 'age' maps to 25.

Formula/usage: dict[key] retrieves the value for a given key.

Practice: Create a dictionary with three items: 'color', 'shape', and 'size', and assign values to them.

3. The 'Indirect' Approach — Prompting for Astra-Level Behavior
You can't download Astra's weights, but you can put ANY capable model (GPT-6 Astra itself via ChatGPT
custom instructions, GPT-4/5-class via API, or Claude) into 'agent mode' with a strong system prompt. The
framework below has five parts. Use all five every time.
ROLE — Define exactly what kind of agent it is and its scope of authority.
CAPABILITIES — List the tools it should assume/use: web search, code execution, file/doc creation,
browsing.
OPERATING MODE — Tell it to plan silently, work in steps, and only report back with results — not narrate
every micro-action.
STANDARDS — Set quality bars: cite sources, verify code runs, ask only when truly blocked, prefer
finishing over asking.
OUTPUT FORMAT — Specify exactly how you want results delivered (files, structured sections,
summaries).
4. Paste-Ready System Prompt
Paste this into ChatGPT's Custom Instructions (or as the system message via API). This configures any
capable model — including GPT-6 Astra — to behave as a general-purpose research/code/docs/browsing
agent.

- You handle complete tasks end-to-end: research, coding, document creation, and web

sources.title: Understanding LLMs & Building an Astra-Style Agent
sources.text:
Understanding LLMs & Building a GPT-6
 Astra-Style Agent
A practical guide: how large language models work, what makes GPT-6 Astra 'agentic', and
a ready-to-use prompt framework to get Astra-level behavior for research, coding,
documents, and browsing tasks.
Prepared for: Ayush  |  Tech Masala
Topic: LLM fundamentals + indirect prompt-based agent replication
1. What Is an LLM, Briefly
A Large Language Model (LLM) is a neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next piece
of text (token) given everything before it. Three things determine what a model can actually do for you in
practice:
●
Base capability — how well it reasons, codes, and recalls facts (set by training).
●
Context window — how much text/files it can hold in memory at once (Astra: ~1.05M tokens).
●
Tools it's connected to — web browsing, code execution, file creation, apps. This is what turns a
'chatbot' into an 'agent'.
The key insight: a lot of what makes a model feel like 'Astra' isn't secret weights you can copy — it's the
combination of (a) a strong base model, (b) tool access, and (c) a system prompt that tells it exactly how to
plan, use tools, and structure output. You can't recreate the base model, but you can recreate most of the
behavior pattern with (b) and (c) — that's the 'indirect' approach.

5. Tuning It For Specific Jobs
Add ONE of these task blocks under the base prompt depending on what you need that session, instead of
rewriting the whole thing each time.
Research task: "Research [topic]. Search at least 5 independent sources, cross-check disputed claims, and
deliver a structured brief with sources listed."
Coding task: "Build [thing]. Write working code, test it mentally or by running it, and deliver the final files —
not just snippets — with a one-line summary of what changed."
Document task: "Create a [doc type] on [topic]. Deliver it as a finished file, formatted and ready to use, not
a draft in chat."
Browsing/current-info task: "Check current [thing] as of today's date. Do not answer from memory —
verify with a live search first."
6. Quick Reality Check
This framework gets you Astra-style behavior — autonomous, multi-step, tool-using, deliverable-focused. It
does not give you Astra's actual underlying model quality (that depends on which model you run the prompt
on) or its native tool integrations (browsing/code execution have to be enabled on whichever platform you
use). For the closest match to real Astra behavior, run this prompt as custom instructions inside ChatGPT
with GPT-6 Astra selected in Work mode, where browsing and code execution are already built in.
